name: Caer Sidi
summary: Arawn's turning gaol on the road to Annwn, where the dead who would not lie down are kept, and the end of all things waits at the top.

facts.text: Caer Sidi is a level 50 Shrouded Isles epic dungeon bordering Caldey.
Arawn, lord of the underworld, sent his Inconnu to help Albion because Morgana was taking his dead to serve her.
In Mythic's Catacombs lore Arawn chose nine Maidens to guard his cauldron, and Morgana stole souls from the Deadlands of Annwn and turned them against him.

Source myth (inspiration only): in the Welsh poem Preiddeu Annwfn, Caer Siddi is a revolving fortress of the otherworld where Gweir lies chained; three shiploads of Arthur's men sailed in Prydwen and only seven came back; a cauldron there, warmed by nine maidens' breath, will not boil a coward's food.
Its dead include crypt knights, custodians, forerunners, reckoned souls, fate's bearers, calcified manes, an archlich and heralds of trucidation.
Apocalypse and four Horsemen (Fames, Bellum, Morbus, Funus) are the final encounter; the Horsemen speak of fate and ask the raid whether it challenges it.
A February 2003 Albion guide put Apocalypse at a minimum of about a hundred players, the author's lowest kill at 105.
Existing bot chat says Caer Sidi sits on the road to Annwn and holds a prison of souls with something at the bottom that keeps the count.

story:
The bards of Albion still sing that Arthur sailed Prydwen to Caer Sidi with three shiploads of men and that seven came home. They sing that the fortress turns, so that few ever find its door, and that whoever lies chained there lies chained for good. The bards were closer to the truth than they knew.

Caer Sidi is Arawn's gaol. Every kingdom of the dead must have a place for the ones who will not go quietly: the oath-breakers, the cowards, the warlords who would not lay down their swords, the priests who wanted to come back. Arawn built it on the road between Albion and Annwn and set keepers in it, crypt knights and custodians, a sacristan for the sacred vessels and a provisioner to feed the dead from a cauldron that will not boil a coward's meat. A reckoner kept the count of every soul that went in. None was meant to come out.

Then Morgana began stealing the dead out of Annwn, and the prisoners of Caer Sidi heard that the door of the underworld could be opened from the wrong side. The gaol rose. Its prisoners made themselves its lords: liches who had been priests, a blood-lord who will not stay dead, a warlord who still drills his knights, a host of eight where only one is real. Arawn's keepers turned with them or were turned.

And at the top of the turning fortress, in the cell Arawn built first and locked last, waits the thing he could not destroy and would not let loose: the end of the world, and the four riders who go before it. They do not attack. They ask a question. Every raid that has ever climbed Caer Sidi has had to answer it.
legend: A hundred for Apocalypse, the old guides said, and the lowest anyone managed was a hundred and five. Never wear anything shiny in Caer Sidi; the dead go for the gilded first. Lich Lord Ilron is where most stories end. At the top, Fames asks if you challenge fate, and you say yes, and then you have two minutes. Everyone remembers those two minutes.

firstEntry: The walls turn slowly. The door you came by is gone.
Caer Sidi. Arawn's gaol. Every cell is open.

loremaster.intro: Caer Sidi? The [bards] sing of it, and the bards are nearly right. It is [Arawn's gaol], and its [prisoners] have made themselves its lords. At the top waits something worse: the [four riders].

topics.bards: Arthur sailed Prydwen to Caer Sidi with three shiploads of men, the old song says, and seven came home. The fortress turns, so few find its door. Remember the number seven before you go.
topics.arawn's gaol: Every kingdom of the dead needs a place for those who will not go quietly. Arawn built his on the road to Annwn and set keepers in it: knights, custodians, a [sacristan], a provisioner, a reckoner who counts.
topics.prisoners: When Morgana began stealing Arawn's dead, the prisoners heard that the door of the underworld could be opened from the wrong side, and they rose. Liches, a blood-lord, a warlord, a host of eight. Ask about [Lich Lord Ilron] if you would know where most tales end.
topics.four riders: Fames, Bellum, Morbus and Funus: Famine, War, Plague and the Funeral, named in the Roman tongue. They go before [Apocalypse]. They will not attack you first. They will ask you a question. Answer it.
topics.apocalypse: The end of the world, locked in the first cell Arawn ever built. He is not angry. He is curious. He will ask you why you came. Bring a hundred, and clerics, and do not lose heart when he takes to the air.
topics.sacristan: The keeper of the sacred vessels. He still walks his round on the high walk, though the vessels are long gone. Stand in his way.
topics.lich lord ilron: Most of the tales I know end at him. He shows you four of himself; only one is true. Find the one that matters.

book.title: The Turning Gaol
pages: Arthur sailed Prydwen to the fortress that turns, so the old song goes, with three shiploads of men, and seven came home. I always took the song for a riddle. Then I stood on the shore beyond Caldey and watched the walls of Caer Sidi move in the dusk, slow as a millstone, and I understood that the bards had been plain. Its door is never where you left it. The Inconnu who guided us said that was the point. A gaol should not be easy to leave.

The Inconnu told us what the place was for. Their lord Arawn keeps the dead, and most of the dead go quietly. Some do not: the oath-breaker, the coward, the warlord who would not lay down his sword, the priest who wanted to come back. Arawn built Caer Sidi for them and gave it keepers. A reckoner to count them in. A provisioner to feed them from a cauldron that will not boil a coward's meat. A sacristan to keep the vessels. Knights to keep the doors.

When the witch began stealing the dead of Annwn, the Inconnu said, the prisoners learned that a door can be opened from the wrong side. They did not escape. They did something worse. They stayed, and made themselves the masters of their own prison. The liches took the galleries. The blood-lord took the chapel. The warlord took the yard and drilled the keepers' own knights. The reckoner went on counting, and no one knows any more for whom.

At the top of the fortress is the first cell Arawn built, and the last he locked. The Inconnu would not say what is in it. They said only that four riders wait before its door, that the riders are courteous, and that they will ask a question. The first of them asked us whether we would challenge fate. One of us laughed. Fames looked at him for a long time, and then told us we had two minutes.
